statement:
Boolean intervals: the complete list of stable types
Let $\mathcal G_{g,n}$ be the poset of isomorphism classes of connected stable weighted graphs with $n$ labelled legs, ordered by $H\leq G$ when $G$ is a contraction of $H$. Every interval is Boolean precisely for the stable types
\[
 (g,n)=(0,n),\quad n\geq3,\qquad\text{and}\qquad(g,n)=(1,1).
\]
For $g=0$ the order-reversing map from a graph to its set of internal-edge splits identifies this poset with the face poset of the complex of compatible stable splits, including the empty face.
This decides Part A(a)(i),(ii) and the first determination requested there; it addresses cote 150, scans 28--30.
notes: Complete stable-type list; graph enumeration is exhaustive from vertex/edge bounds.

statement:
Infima of pairs with a common lower bound
Every pair in $\mathcal G_{g,n}$ having a common lower bound has an infimum precisely for
\[
 g=0,\ n\geq3;\qquad g=1,\ 1\leq n\leq3;\qquad(g,n)=(2,0).
\]
In particular the two divisors $\Delta_{\mathrm{irr}}$ and $\Delta_1$ in type $(2,1)$ have two distinct maximal common lower bounds. The infimum assertion and the Boolean assertion therefore have different lists, related by the explicit graph constructions below.
notes: Complete infimum list, uniform counterexamples, exhaustive certificates in the four positive-genus cases.

statement:
Intersection and the Boolean deployment of a fixed contraction
For closed strata $X_G$ one has
\[
 X_G\cap X_{G'}=\bigcup_{H\leq G,\ H\leq G'}X_H.
\]
For a specified contraction $f:G\to G/C$, its intermediate factorizations, modulo isomorphisms of the intermediate graph commuting with both arrows, form the Boolean poset of subsets of $C$. This assertion holds in every stable type, including those excluded in A.1.
notes: The graph and the contraction are fixed before the factorization quotient.

statement:
The category with graph objects and its associative composition
Choose a multicurve $\sigma_G$ of each dual-graph type $G$. Define
\[
 \Hom_{\mathfrak M(g,n)}(G,H)
 =\{a\in\Gamma:a\sigma_G\supseteq\sigma_H\}/\Delta_{\sigma_G},
 \qquad [b]\circ[a]=[ba].
\]
This defines an EI category. Different choices of the $\sigma_G$ give equivalent categories by explicitly specified conjugation functors. The category on all multicurves with the same formula is equivalent to this finite-object skeleton.
notes: Right transporter cosets; explicit conjugation functors for changes of representatives.

statement:
Pinned strata, asphericity, and injective meridian lattices
For a stable graph $G$ with half-edge/leg set $I_v$ at vertex $v$, simultaneous normalization gives an equivalence of analytic stacks
\[
 M_G\simeq\prod_{v\in V(G)}\mathcal M_{g_v,I_v}.
\]
The unpinned stratum is $[M_G/\Aut G]$. It is aspherical as a stack, and for a multicurve $\sigma$ with graph $G$,
\[
 \pi_1([M_G/\Aut G])\cong\Stab_\Gamma(\sigma)/\Delta_\sigma,
 \qquad \Delta_\sigma\cong\Z^{\sigma}.
\]
In particular the meridian lattice injects in the open mapping class group. The extension of cote 147, (103), scan 80, has the asserted initial $1$ for every relative set of nodes. This proves (95), with its stated outer ambiguity.

statement:
The exact arrow-groupoid comparison and the pinning restriction
Let $\sigma\supseteq\tau$, put $S_{\sigma,\tau}=\Stab(\sigma)\cap\Stab(\tau)$, and let $a=[1]:\sigma\to\tau$ be the associated exit arrow. In the groupoid of arrows and invertible endpoint squares, its automorphism group is
\[
 \Aut(a)=S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\tau.
\]
The source and target functors induce respectively
\[
 S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\tau\longrightarrow
 S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\sigma\subseteq\Stab(\sigma)/\Delta_\sigma,
 \qquad
 S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\tau\hookrightarrow\Stab(\tau)/\Delta_\tau.
\]
The first map has kernel $\Delta_\sigma/\Delta_\tau=\Z^{\sigma\setminus\tau}$. These are the maps $\varphi$ and $\gamma$ in (103) for the unpinned incidence. For a target pinned by $G'$, replace $S_{\sigma,\tau}$ everywhere by the inverse image of $\Gamma^!_{G,G'}$, equivalently by the subgroup inducing the identity on the target dual graph. Fully pinning the source imposes the additional identity action on $G$. The corresponding restrictions and inclusions give the comparison with the manuscript's differently pinned versions.

notes: Exact pinning subgroups and both endpoint maps; no identification of differently pinned groups.

statement:
The MDT category, full flags, and Jansen's theorem
The coherent generization system of (103), with its full flags, reconstructs the category of A.4. This category is equivalent to the exit-path $\infty$-category of the stable-graph stratification of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^{\mathrm{an}}$, and its classifying space is the homotopy type of that stack. For a flag $\sigma_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\sigma_r$, the automorphism group of the corresponding composable chain is
\[
 \left(\bigcap_{i=0}^r\Stab(\sigma_i)\right)/\Delta_{\sigma_r}.
\]
The two-cartesian law for composable arrow groupoids gives (105); composition is the map forgetting intermediate objects. Forgetting an intermediate graph need not be an equivalence of mixed groupoids.

notes: Full flags give coherent composition. The composite-link forgetful map can have index two.

statement:
A finite criterion deciding each immersion in (98)
For a specified contraction $f:G\to G'$, the proper gluing map
\[
 [\widehat M_G/\Aut_{G'}G]\longrightarrow\widehat M_{G'}
\]
is a representable finite local closed immersion. For a refinement $h:H\to G'$, form the finite set
\[
 B_f(H,h)=\{p:H\to G:f p=h\}/\Aut_{G'}G.
\]
Here the graph $H$ and its pinning over $G'$ are fixed; we do not quotient this set by automorphisms of $H$. The gluing map is a closed immersion exactly when $|B_f(H,h)|\leq1$ for every refinement. This is a finite decision criterion for every $(g,n)$ and every $f$. Every such map is a closed immersion for genus zero and for $(1,1)$. In every other stable type some such map is only a local immersion, first in dimension two at $(1,2)$.

notes: Finite retained-node criterion; target-object pinning is fixed in the fibre and is not further divided by Aut(H).

statement:
Normalization variance and formula (146)
Strict normalization of a pinned stable graph induces an equivalence of its moduli stack; disjoint union induces the product equivalence (133). For a general normalization morphism $G'\to G$, the contravariant map on pinned moduli is, in the product coordinates of A.5, the projection to the selected vertex factors followed by the forgetful maps of their selected marked points. This proves (144), (146), and the reduction to (148), with natural isomorphisms commuting with relabelling.
notes: Strict normalization, component products, selected components/markings and diagram (146).

statement:
The precise interchange and clutching coherence
For disjoint sets of nodes $C,J$, smoothing $C$ and normalizing $J$ commute through the canonical identification of their component families and remaining sections. Forgetting marked points and then stabilizing gives the commuting functor square with every generization constructed in C.1 below. Clutching pairs of labelled sections, both on distinct components and on one component, and relabelling define the modular operations on the exit categories, with their canonical associativity and equivariance isomorphisms. All coherence diagrams commute. For genus-zero boundary inclusions this recovers the replete full cosieve in entrance variance; in higher genus the clutching normalization has exactly the incidence multiplicities of A.8.
notes: Canonical clutching comparisons; see A.15 for the complete domain of a graph interchange square.

statement:
The simultaneous raw-face assertions in Part A(e)
The definition of $\Sigma_{G_0\to\cdots\to G_k}$ as the corresponding face of the real oriented blow-up does not satisfy all of Part A(e)(i)--(v). With literal oriented faces, (ii) and (iv) already fail for $(0,4)$. With ordinary strata as the object spaces, a link-to-open map is not the boundary-face immersion asserted in (iii). The correct complete Segal space is
\[
 W_r=N\bigl(\Fun([r],\mathcal E_{g,n})^{\simeq}\bigr),
\]
with homotopy-cartesian concatenation maps. Its arrow components are the relative link groupoids of A.6, and its homotopy category is $\mathfrak M(g,n)$.

statement:
Local triviality of the whole deployed family and its lattice monodromy
Over each pinned stratum, the entire normal-crossings family of faces is locally trivial as a stratified family in the analytic topology. For the unpinned stratum, the monodromy of the node set and of its integral angular lattice is
\[
 \pi_1([M_G/\Aut G])\longrightarrow\Aut G
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Perm}(E(G))
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(\Z^{E(G)}).
\]
It permutes the positive Dehn-twist generators. The normal line at an edge $e=\{h,h'\}$ is $T_h\otimes T_{h'}$, with first Chern class $-\psi_h-\psi_{h'}$ on the pinned product stratum. These classes describe the angular torus extensions; local triviality does not assert a global splitting.

A fixed unpinned flag need not give the cartesian square

replacing raw oriented faces by their correct relative link groupoids.
At type $(3,0)$ a homotopy fibre product of two specified incidence
components has two connected components, while a specified full flag
selects one. The homotopy-cartesian formula holds for the disjoint union
of all matching full flags, as in A.7. It also holds with the matching
intermediate pinning retained.

statement:
Deriving ordinariness from the two local inputs
For every stable $(g,n)$, the asphericity and meridian injection in
A.5 imply that every exit mapping space is a disjoint union of
contractible components. This gives the application of EXIT\_ONE\_TYPE
P1b1 requested in added task 1, before invoking Jansen's global
identification. That identification supplies the explicit transporter
formula and its compatibility over all incidences.

statement:
Exactly when graph normalization and contraction have a square
Let $j:G'\to G$ be a normalization morphism in the sense of cote 147,
and let $q:G\to G/C$ be a contraction. Put
$C'=j^{-1}(C)\cap E(G')$ and $H'=G'/C'$. A commutative square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
G'\arrow[r,"j"]\arrow[d]&G\arrow[d,"q"]\\
H'\arrow[r,dashed,"\bar j"]&G/C
\end{tikzcd}
\]
with horizontal normalization morphisms exists exactly when the
following finite tests hold: the induced vertex map is injective,
the genus at every source vertex equals that at its image, and no
retained marked half-edge or leg of $H'$ has been erased by $q$.
The induced maps of the remaining labels must have the incidences
specified in the definition of a normalization morphism; this is
checked directly on the surviving half-edges. When these tests hold,
$\bar j$ is unique, and the associated normalization and relative
generization groupoids form a commuting square up to a canonical
isomorphism. The comparisons are coherent under further admissible
compositions. An unrestricted such square for every pair is false,
already for the strict normalization and smoothing of the single
loop in type $(1,1)$.
notes: Finite criterion for a normalization-contraction square; single-loop counterexample to an unrestricted square.

statement:
The framed torsor and its two quotients
For a pinned stable graph $G$, put
\[
 P_G=\prod_{j\in J(G),\,M_G} U(L_j),\qquad
 L_i=T_{x_i}C\quad(i\in I(G)),\qquad
 L_e=T_{x_h}C_{v(h)}\otimes T_{x_{\bar h}}C_{v(\bar h)}.
\]
Here $U(L)=L^{\times}/\mathbb R_{>0}$ is the oriented unit-ray circle
bundle; no Hermitian metric is required.  We write
$P_G^E=\prod_{e\in E(G)}U(L_e)$.  Choose a finite set $B_G$ in the
pinned stratum, a nonempty finite set of rays above each member of
$B_G$, and saturate the rays under
$\mu_G=\{\pm1\}^{J(G)}$.  Denote the resulting finite set by $D_G$.
When a graph action is required, take $B_G$ invariant and also
saturate $D_G$ under the finite group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
For vertices of genus zero and valence three or four, the groupoid
\[
 \mathcal S_G:=\Pi_1(P_G,D_G)
\]
is a $\mu_G$-free $\mathbb Z^{J(G)}$-groupoid, and its internal lattice
acts freely on every nonempty Hom-set.  Its geometric quotients are
\[
 \mathcal S_G/(\mathbb Z^{I(G)},\mu_2^{I(G)})
       \simeq\Pi_1(P_G^E,\operatorname{im}D_G),
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_G/(\mathbb Z^{J(G)},\mu_G)
       \simeq\Pi_1(M_G,B_G).
 \tag{B.1}
\]
The first groupoid has the node-framed link group of Part A.  The
second has automorphism group $\prod_{v:\,|F_v|=4}F_2$.  After choices
of trivializations, the automorphism group of $\mathcal S_G$ is
\[
 \mathbb Z^{J(G)}\times\prod_{v:\,|F_v|=4}F_2.
 \tag{B.2}
\]
The direct-product splitting in (B.2) is not specified as
$\operatorname{Aut}(G)$-equivariant.
notes: Topological circle bundles, labelled pinned rational components; graph action obtained by invariant finite ray saturation. Exact flag-to-edge tensor map and both lattice/sign quotients.

statement:
The presentation actually written in scans 115--117
For a trivalent rational graph set $r=|J(G)|$.  The finite model of
cote 146, scans 114--117 (folios 113--116), has the $2^r$ objects of
the sign torsor $D_G=\prod_{j\in J(G)}\varepsilon_j$.  It has
$r2^r$ positive half-turn generators
\[
 u_{j,x}:x\longrightarrow\sigma_jx
 \quad(j\in J(G),\ x\in D_G).
\]
Its relations are the source-compatible commuting squares for two
different coordinates.  The commutation of the full-turn loops
$v_{j,x}=u_{j,\sigma_jx}u_{j,x}$ written on scan 117 follows from
these squares.  Equivalently,
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}(x,y)=
 \{m\in\mathbb Z^r:m\bmod2=y-x\},
 \tag{B.4}
\]
where addition gives composition and $m$ records displacement in
units of a half turn.  The loop lattice is $2\mathbb Z^r$, identified
with $\mathbb Z^r$ by $2e_j\mapsto e_j$.

statement:
The proposed equivalence before forgetting leg framings
The proposed equivalence $S_0\mathcal T_G\simeq S_A\Pi M_G$ without
quotienting the leg framings is false, already for the graph with
one trivalent rational vertex and three labelled legs.  The exact
comparison is the first functor in (B.1), whose kernel at every
object is $\mathbb Z^{I(G)}$.

statement:
The genus-zero tree index and the chart counts
The category of reduced stable trees with a fixed individually
labelled leaf set, and specified edge contractions fixing those
labels, is equivalent to a finite poset.  On four and five leaves,
the numbers of trees by number of internal edges are respectively
$(1,3)$ and $(1,10,15)$.  For the disjoint union of their trivalent
charts, the scan 116 presentations have the following counts;
these counts precede any global identification of chart objects.
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r|r}

       &\text{node-only objects / generators}\\\hline
 4&3&5&96&480&6\,/\,6\\

\end{array}
\tag{B.5}
\]

statement:
Freeness does not follow from an unspecified finite colimit
The implication that a finite colimit of groupoids with a free
$\mu_2$-action on objects has a free action on objects is false.
Consequently that implication alone cannot justify the sentence
following the first formula of cote 146, scan 100.
notes: Finite equivariant coequalizer of the indiscrete two-object C2-groupoid has one fixed object. Addresses a general colimit inference, not a specified manuscript index.

statement:
An explicit obstruction for the boundary-incidence interpretation
Let $L$ be the boundary of a sufficiently small regular
neighbourhood of the boundary divisor in $\overline M_{0,5}$.  The
colimit of the fundamental groupoids of its circle-bundle pieces
and all their torus intersections presents $\Pi_1(L)$.  The inclusion
$L\to M_{0,5}$ does not induce an isomorphism of fundamental groups.
Thus this specified boundary-incidence colimit cannot be the
missing global presentation in scan 100.
notes: Specified boundary-incidence colimit gives an aspherical closed3-manifold group with H3=Z; M0,5 has a2-dimensional K(pi,1), H3=0. No attribution of that index to the manuscript.

statement:
The precise relation to the Lego groupoid
Let $\mathcal L(\Sigma)$ be the marking two-complex of
Bakalov--Kirillov with their moves and relations, and let $\Gamma$
be the mapping class group with the same orientation and boundary
conventions.  The groupoid with objects the markings and arrows
\[
 M\longrightarrow M':\quad (g,[p]),\qquad
 g\in\Gamma,\quad p:gM\leadsto M',
\]
is equivalent to $B\Gamma$ by $(g,[p])\mapsto g$.  With fixed labels
and capped boundary circles it gives the open groupoid
$B\Gamma_{0,n}$ in Part A.  The capping functor kills exactly the
central lattice of boundary twists.
notes: Exact equivariant marking groupoid functor to BΓ, with composition, capping map and boundary-twist kernel; BK Theorem4.9 reopened.

statement:
The finite-colimit assertion with its specified comparison maps
The mathematical finite-colimit assertion of original scan100 has
the explicit realizations B.27--B.30.  B.27 gives a strict finite
geometric diagram, its comparison and inverse, and a reduced
labelled-tree index in genus zero.  B.29 supplies the cubic and
quartic covering functors, every boundary half turn, and the
elliptic cut-change relations.  B.30 gives a sphere-only finite
diagram with explicit continuous path functors, a free sign action,
and an ordered index after finite coproducts.  Its generator
substitutions compare it with B.27 and the marked-pants model.

The individual finite object choices and transition representatives
intended by the unfinished last phrase of scan100 are a source
uncertainty, retained in the reading register.  The constructions
just stated specify their own choices and every comparison map;
the existence theorem does not depend on recovering an unrecorded
choice.  The early four-point model is reconstructed in B.16--B.17,
and B.15 and B.31 give the exact choice-independent comparison for
the full five-point diagram.

statement:
Finite presentation yields a finite colimit of elementary framed groupoids
For each pinned stable graph, its framed fundamental groupoid admits
a finite-colimit presentation in the category of groupoids with its
specified central lattice and finite sign action.  One may take the
elementary automorphism groups, after changing the central lattice,
to be $\mathbb Z^r$ and $\mathbb Z^r\times F_2$, the groups of the
three- and four-point rational pieces.  The arrows in this colimit
are the word maps specified below.  This proves existence of a
finite algebraic presentation of the asserted kind.  It does not
identify these word maps with the unfinished tree-indexed diagram
of scan 100.
notes: Finite colimit built from explicit word maps in central extensions, with identity object maps preserving free sign action. Establishes abstract existence, not the original tree diagram.

statement:
The two open groupoids and their leg-framed extensions
For complex curves with individually labelled markings,
\[
 \Gamma_{1,1}=\langle a,b\mid aba=bab,\ (ab)^6=1\rangle
                 \cong\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z),
 \tag{B.8}
\]
\[
 \Gamma_{1,2}=\langle a,b,c\mid aba=bab,\ bcb=cbc,
               \ ac=ca,\ (abc)^4=1\rangle.
 \tag{B.9}
\]
Thus $\Pi_1M_{1,n}$ is equivalent to the one-object groupoid on the
displayed group.  The groups of the unit tangent-ray bundles at
all marked points are respectively
\[
 H_{1,1}=\langle a,b\mid aba=bab\rangle,
       \qquad z_1=(ab)^6,
 \tag{B.10}
\]
and
\[
 H_{1,2}=\left\langle a,b,c,z_1,z_2\ \middle|\
 \begin{array}{l}
 aba=bab,\ bcb=cbc,\ ac=ca,\\
 z_1,z_2\text{ central},\ (abc)^4=z_1z_2
 \end{array}\right\rangle
 \cong B_4\times\mathbb Z.
 \tag{B.11}
\]
Here $z_i$ is the positive full turn at the $i$th marked point.
The capping maps are the quotients $z_i\mapsto1$.
notes: Γ1,1=B3/<(ab)^6>; Γ1,2=B4/<(abc)^4>; framed H1,1=B3, H1,2=B4×Z with δ^4=z1z2. Independent cubic/quartic quotient construction and LP chain words.

statement:
All boundary graph groups in these two types
For $(1,1)$ there is one boundary graph: a rational vertex with one
loop and one labelled leg.  Its pinned stratum is a point and its
mixed stratum is $BC_2$.  Put $h=(ab)^3$.  Its fully framed mixed
link group is
\[
 \langle a,h\mid[a,h]=1\rangle,\qquad z_1=h^2.
 \tag{B.12}
\]
Its node-only mixed link group is
$\langle a,h\mid[a,h]=1,h^2=1\rangle$.

For $(1,2)$ name the four boundary graph types as follows:
$N$ is a rational vertex with a loop and both legs;
$T$ is an elliptic vertex joined to a rational tail carrying both
legs; $C$ is a two-edge rational cycle with one labelled leg on
each vertex; and $D$ is a rational loop vertex joined to a rational
tail carrying both legs.  Write
\[
 s=aba,\quad\Delta=abcaba,\quad
 r=s^{-1}\Delta s,\quad q=(abc)^2,\quad h=(ab)^3,
 \quad d=h^2.
 \tag{B.13}
\]
The pinned stratum groups are $F_2$, $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$,
$1$, $1$ for $N,T,C,D$, respectively.  The mixed stratum groups are
$C_2*\mathbb Z$, $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$, $C_2$, $C_2$.
The following are presentations of their fully framed mixed link
groups; in every row $z_1,z_2$ are central:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|l}
 \text{graph}&\text{generators and additional relations}
                   &\text{node twists}\\\hline
 N&a,c,r,z_1,z_2;\ [a,c]=[a,r]=1,\ r^2=z_1z_2&a\\
 T&a,b,z_1,z_2;\ aba=bab&d=(ab)^6\\
 C&a,c,q,z_1,z_2;\ [a,c]=1,\ qaq^{-1}=c,\ q^2=z_1z_2&a,c\\
 D&a,h,z_1,z_2;\ [a,h]=1&a,d=h^2
\end{array}
\tag{B.14}
\]
The pinned full-framing subgroups are the kernels of the graph
permutation: in rows $N,C,D$ the respective quotient maps send
$r,q,h$ to the nonidentity member of $C_2$, and all lattice
coordinates to the identity.  The graph group in row $T$ is
trivial.  The node-only link groups are obtained by $z_1=z_2=1$.
The mixed stratum groups are obtained by also killing the listed
node twists.
notes: All stable boundary graphs in(1,1),(1,2), pinned/mixed groups and full node-plus-leg-framed extensions. Finite graph involutions retained.

statement:
Generization on every boundary flag in the two small genera
The generization maps from the groups (B.12)--(B.14) to the open
framed groups are the inclusions specified by the words (B.13).
In $(1,2)$ the two nontrivial two-step flags, in addition to the
cycle flags, have maps
\[
 D\longrightarrow T:\quad a\mapsto a,\ h\mapsto(ab)^3,
 \qquad
 D\longrightarrow N:\quad a\mapsto a,\ h\mapsto ac^{-1}r,
 \tag{B.15}
\]
with $z_i\mapsto z_i$.  For $C\to N$ retaining the node $a$, the
arrow-stabilizer group is the subgroup
$\langle a,c,z_1,z_2\rangle$ of row $C$, and its map to row $N$ is
the identity on these named generators.  The other contraction is
its conjugate by $q$.  These maps compose to the maximal
generization maps.  After the lattice quotients in B.10 they give
the corresponding pinned and mixed groupoid spans of Part A.
notes: Explicit braid words for every low-type flag; cycle contractions restricted to their correct arrow stabilizers.12 Artin-action checks pass.

statement:
The nine vertex orbits and the corrected sixteen arrow orbits
Let $K$ be a fixed five-element set and let $\mathfrak S_K$ act by
relabeling.  The vertex sets of cote 148, scan 31, are the following
nine transitive $\mathfrak S_K$-sets.  The symbols in the first column
are the manuscript's symbols; subscripts are stabilizer orders.
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|r}
\text{type}&\text{stabilizer in }S_5&\text{number}\\ \hline
\mathrm I_{10}&D_5&12\\
\mathrm I_6&S_3\text{ acting on }3+2\text{ by its sign}&20\\
\mathrm I_4&C_4&30\\
\mathrm {II}_2&C_2&60\\
\mathrm {II}'_2&C_2&60\\
\mathrm {II}_1&1&120\\
\mathrm {III}_2&C_2&60\\
\mathrm {III}_1&1&120\\
\mathrm {III}'_2&C_2&60
\end{array}
\tag{B.16}
\]
In every $C_2$ row the nonidentity element is a double
transposition.  Thus the number of vertices is $542$, in nine
orbits.  The fourteen named arrow families have the following
cardinalities and orbit decompositions:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|r|r}
\text{family}&\text{source and target}&\text{arrows}&S_5\text{-orbits}\\ \hline
 f_{B,s}&\mathrm I_6\to\mathrm I_4&60&1\\
 f_{\vec Q,a}&\mathrm {II}'_2\to\mathrm I_4&120&1\\

outer boundary, let $T_0,\ldots,T_4$ be the five binary planar

 A_4A_3A_2A_1A_0=1_{T_0}. \tag{B.18}

Finite chamber arrows reduced to pure moduli generators

with objects the $m!$ orderings $w$ of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and arrows

\[
 z_m=(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{m-1})^m.                 \tag{B.25}
\]
Then $\mathcal C_m\simeq\Pi_1M_{0,m+1}$.  The comparison is induced
by the actual adjacent half-turn paths in the ordered configuration

\end{array}                                                   \tag{B.26}
\]

             \sigma_{i+1}^{-1}\cdots\sigma_{j-1}^{-1},
 \qquad 1\leq i<j\leq m,\quad (i,j)\ne(1,2).       \tag{B.27}

statement:
A strict finite colimit with the five elementary types
Let $S$ be an oriented stable surface with individually labelled
boundary circles $I$, let $H=\Gamma(S,\partial S)$, and put
$A=\mathbb Z^I$, with its positive boundary-twist generators.
There is a strict finite diagram of finite-object groupoids,
with a free action of $\mu=A/2A$ on their object sets, whose
ordinary colimit is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of
the full tangent-ray bundle of the corresponding moduli stack,
restricted to the specified finite rays.  The equivalence
preserves the boundary half-turns and full turns.

The pieces are obtained by cutting and sewing from the five
types
\[
 (0,3),\quad(0,4),\quad(0,5),\quad(1,1),\quad(1,2). \tag{B.74}
\]
For genus zero the index can be the finite poset of reduced
labelled trees $G$ with
\[
 \sum_v(\operatorname{val}(v)-3)\leq2,
\]
ordered by edge contraction.  The local five-point and elliptic
pieces here are the explicitly presented groupoids of B.19,
B.25 and B.9--B.11.  For a pinned graph with several vertices,
finite products and the flag-to-edge induction of B.1 give the
same result with the full external lattice
$\mathbb Z^{E(G)\amalg I(G)}$.

This proves a geometric finite-colimit recipe with all five

of only three- and four-point sphere pieces, nor identify an
unstated original finite ray convention.  B.29--B.30 supply explicit

 Q:\mathcal E_{g,n+1}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_{g,n},

statement:
Restriction to the open fibre and the automorphism comparison
Let $U_r=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\setminus\{r\text{ labelled points}\}$, $r\geq3$, and give $\mathbb P^1$ the stratification by those points and their complement. Its strict completed exit category has one open object with group $\widehat\pi_r=\widehat F_{r-1}$, $r$ closed objects with trivial groups, and crossing sets $\widehat\pi_r/I_i$, where $I_i$ is the peripheral procyclic subgroup. Restriction to the open object induces an isomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{eq},I}(\widehat{\Exit}(\mathbb P^1,r))
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \Out_I(\widehat\pi_r).                                    \tag{C.3}
\]
The left group is autoequivalences modulo natural isomorphism, preserving the labelled closed objects; on both sides we impose the same common multiplier on the chosen positive inertia generators. Allowing permutation of the labels gives the corresponding permuting version. These fibre exit categories occur in the universal stable-curve functors. Formula (C.3) is the map relating LM3b's surface-group automorphisms to the completed categories in this paper.

statement:
An explicit full-profinite filling kernel in every spherical size
Let $r\geq3$, let $F=\widehat F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{r-1})$, set $p=xy_1\cdots y_{r-1}$, and put $\bar F=F/\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle=\widehat F(y_1,\ldots,y_{r-1})$. Let $O_{r+1,x}$ consist of peripheral-preserving outer automorphisms of $F$ fixing the distinguished puncture $x$, with a common unit multiplier, and let $O_r$ be the analogous group on $\bar F$. Filling and normalized filling are continuous surjections
\[
 f_x:O_{r+1,x}\twoheadrightarrow O_r,
 \qquad\theta_x:O_{r+1,x}\twoheadrightarrow\Aut_I(\bar F).
\]
Let $K\cong\bar F$ be the point-pushing subgroup. Then
\[
 \ker f_x=Q_r\rtimes K,\qquad Q_r\ne1.                      \tag{C.4}
\]
The following word model specifies $Q_r$ without a kernel notation. Put $N=\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle$. Take tuples $(w_1,\ldots,w_{r-1},w_\infty)\in N^r$ satisfying
\[
 x\prod_{j=1}^{r-1}w_j^{-1}y_jw_j=w_\infty^{-1}p w_\infty,   \tag{C.5}
\]
and the finite test that, in every finite quotient $F\twoheadrightarrow H$,
the images of the following elements generate $H$:
\[
 x,\quad w_1^{-1}y_1w_1,\quad\ldots,\quad
 w_{r-1}^{-1}y_{r-1}w_{r-1}.
\]
Denote the substitution they define by $\alpha_w$. The product is
\[
 (w*v)_j=w_j\alpha_w(v_j),\qquad
 (w*v)_\infty=w_\infty\alpha_w(v_\infty).
\]
Quotient by simultaneous right multiplication of all $w_j,w_\infty$ by $x^a$, $a\in\widehat\Z$. With its quotient profinite topology this is $Q_r$. Thus (C.4)--(C.5) give, in particular, the kernels of the fillings $4\to3$ and $5\to4$ as explicit profinite groups.

statement:
What the three bridge groups contribute at $5\to4$

Its image is the procyclic subgroup generated by pushing around the corresponding two-versus-two separating curve; the original $\Z$ has dense cyclic image in it. Their closed normal closure inside $K$ has quotient $C_2$. Their intersection with $Q_4$ is trivial. Thus their actual contribution to the filling kernel in (C.4) lies entirely in its geometric point-pushing factor. The extra factor $Q_3\ne1$ already occurs for $4\to3$, where C.2 gives no bridge group.

statement:
The nonorientable comparison and real-equivariant representatives
For a compact smooth nonorientable surface, the inclusion of
diffeomorphisms into homeomorphisms induces an isomorphism of
mapping-class groups, also with individually fixed marked points
and boundary fixed pointwise. For a closed nonorientable surface
$N_h$ with $h$ crosscaps, the unmarked identity components in both
categories have homotopy types
\[
 SO(3)\quad(h=1),\qquad S^1\quad(h=2),\qquad *\quad(h\geq3).
\]
With one fixed point $N_1$ has identity component of weak homotopy
type $S^1$; with at least two it is weakly contractible.
For $N_2$ with at least one fixed point, and for $N_h$ with
$h\geq3$ with any number of fixed points, it is weakly contractible.

Let $\tau$ be a specified smooth orientation-reversing involution
of an oriented compact surface, and retain a specified finite
$\tau$-invariant marking. The inclusion of the smooth centralizer
of $\tau$ into its topological centralizer induces an isomorphism
on component groups, with the same marking conditions. Quotient
and lift along $S\to S/\langle\tau\rangle$ give the comparison.

statement:
Compactification independence of the two end constructions
For any compact Hausdorff compactification $U\subset X$ with $D=X\setminus U$, the archimedean punctured-neighborhood pro-space is canonically the end system $\{U\setminus K\}_{K\subset U\text{ compact}}$. \[
 W(X',X'\setminus U)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }W(X,D),\qquad
 W(X,D)=X^{\beth}\setminus(U^{\beth}\cup D^{\beth}).
\]

statement:
The corrected maquette and its comparison fibres
Let $\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+}$ be the category of stable labelled graphs with at least one edge, with specified contractions and graph isomorphisms as morphisms. Define
\[
 \mathcal B_p=
 \{\,(G,\lambda):|E(G)|=p+1,\ 
       \lambda:E(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{0,\ldots,p\}\,\}/\cong .
\]
Relabelling gives the symmetric-group action; an injection of label sets gives a face by contracting precisely the omitted edges. Then $\mathcal B$ is a symmetric semisimplicial set, its realization is the boundary complex, and the map assigning the label weights to the edge lengths is a homeomorphism
\[
 |\mathcal B|\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_{g,n}.
\]
Here $\Delta_{g,n}$ is the space of stable tropical curves of total finite-edge length one. The category with the automorphisms retained has the explicit comparison
\[
 B\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+}\simeq
 \operatorname*{hocolim}_{(\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+})^{\rm op}}\Delta_G
 \longrightarrow
 \operatorname*{colim}_{(\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+})^{\rm op}}\Delta_G
 =\Delta_{g,n},\qquad
 \Delta_G=\{(\ell_e)\geq0:\sum\ell_e=1\}.
\]
The actual point fibre of this homotopy-colimit model over a metric graph $(G,\ell)$ has homotopy type $B\operatorname{Aut}(G,\ell)$. The map need not be a quasifibration; this assertion concerns its actual point fibres. Adding the zero-edge graph makes the full graph category contractible, since that graph is terminal.

The analytic boundary end has a compatible comparison to these models. Over a positive-length metric multicurve $(\sigma,\ell)$, the point fibre of its Borel-model map to $\Delta_{g,n}$ is
$B\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma_{g,n}}(\sigma,\ell)$.
The map of that fibre to the graph-model fibre is induced by the graph-action homomorphism, whose kernel is the node-framed pure cut-surface group. In particular its homotopy fibre is the classifying space of that kernel.

The exact word problem, flag index and four stabilizer families for $(1,3)$
Write $a_1,a_2,a_3$ for three mutually disjoint parallel
nonseparating curves, with one marked point in each intervening
annulus, and let $b$ meet each once.  Label $p_i$ as the point
opposite $a_i$ in the standard star picture.  There is the
explicit presentation
\[
 \Gamma_{1,3}=
 \left\langle a_1,a_2,a_3,b\ \middle|\
 [a_i,a_j]=1,\ a_i b a_i=b a_i b,\
 \Delta=(a_1a_2a_3b)^3=1\right\rangle.                       \tag{D.22}
\]
The maps send the four letters to exactly these Dehn twists.
The executed classical Garside algorithm in
\path{code/d_artin_d4.py} solves its word problem by computing
in $A(D_4)$ and retaining the proper greedy factors after
removing the central $\Delta$ exponent.

For $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$, put
\[
 d_i=(a_jba_k)^4,\qquad q_i=a_jba_k a_jba_j.
\]
Then $d_i$ is the separating twist enclosing $p_j,p_k$,
and the following are exact stabilizers with literal
embeddings into (D.22):
\[
\begin{split}
 G_{\{d_i\}}&=B_4(a_j,b,a_k),\\
 G_{\{a_j,a_k\}}&=
 \langle a_1,a_2,a_3,q_i\mid [a_r,a_s]=1,
 q_i a_jq_i^{-1}=a_k,\ q_i a_kq_i^{-1}=a_j,
 (q_i a_i)^2=a_ja_k\rangle,\\
 G_{\{a_j,a_k,d_i\}}&=
 \langle a_j,a_k,q_i\mid[a_j,a_k]=1,
 q_i a_jq_i^{-1}=a_k,\ q_i a_kq_i^{-1}=a_j\rangle,\\
 G_{\{a_1,a_2,a_3\}}&=\mathbb Z^3(a_1,a_2,a_3).
\end{split}                                                       \tag{D.23}
\]
In both middle lines $q_i^2=d_i$; in the third line this
is the separating meridian, not an imposed order-two
relation.  These four families give ten of the twenty-two
vertex-orbit stabilizers.

The complete finite flag index has $22$ vertices, $53$ edges
and $33$ triangles.  Thus the barycentric complex of groups
has $108$ objects, $304$ face arrows and $198$ coherence
triangles.  Every orbit and its actual retained-edge subsets
is listed in \path{code/d_p2_elliptic_three_partial.json}.
D.29 supplies all the remaining named local maps and
completes the full dictionary.  This result records the
exact word algorithm and the four foundational families.

Every level measures an explicit quotient of the congruence kernel
Fix a stable type $(g,n)$, put $d=3g-3+n$, and retain
$K=K_{g,n}$ from (D.40).  For an actual multicurve $\sigma$,
let $S_v$ be its cut components, with types $(g_v,n_v)$
including the individually pinned node branches.
There is a natural continuous homomorphism
\[
 \kappa_\sigma:\prod_v K_{g_v,n_v}
                  \longrightarrow K\subset\widehat\Gamma_{g,n}
                                                               \tag{D.55}
\]
defined by the cutting diagrams below.  Its image is exactly
$K\cap\overline{C_\sigma}$, where $C_\sigma$ is the actual
discrete multicurve stabilizer and the bar is closure in
$\widehat\Gamma_{g,n}$.

For $k\geq2$, let $J_k$ be the closed normal subgroup of $K$
generated by all the subgroups
\[
 h\,\operatorname{im}(\kappa_\sigma)h^{-1},
 \qquad h\in\widehat\Gamma_{g,n},\qquad
                         |\sigma|\geq d-k.                  \tag{D.56}
\]
Only one representative of each actual multicurve orbit is
needed in this formula.  The empty multicurve is included
when $k\geq d$; its map (D.55) is the identity of $K$.
Then there is a continuous group isomorphism, with the usual
inner ambiguity from the basepoint,
\[
               \Pi_1(\check P_k)\ \cong\ K/J_k.             \tag{D.57}
\]
Every finite continuous representation of the right side
corresponds explicitly to a finite covering of $\check P_k$
by the quotient construction in the proof.

For $2\leq k\leq6$ and $k<d$, all component kernels in
(D.55) vanish and (D.57) is exactly D.32.  For $k\geq d$
it is the trivial group.  At every intermediate level,
(D.55)--(D.57) specify the remaining kernel equation without
asserting its vanishing.  Inclusions of levels induce the
actual quotient maps $K/J_k\to K/J_{k+1}$, since
$J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}$.

statement:
Higher finite-level connectivity in genera zero, one and two
Let $Y_k=P_k^{\rm lev}$ denote the full level completion and put
$d=3g-3+n$.  For every stable type of genus at most two, the natural
map $Y_k\to\check P_k$ is the canonical isomorphism of D.19.
For $k\geq d$ these profinite spaces are contractible.  For
$0\leq k<d$ the following assertions hold.

In genus zero or one their connectivity is exactly $k-1$.
In genus two their connectivity is at least $-1,0,1$ at
$k=0,1,2$, respectively, and at least $k-2$ for $k\geq3$.
In particular the full nonempty curve complex has profinite
connectivity at least $h(g,n)-1$ in all these genera.
The requested four low types have the following \emph{exact}
connectivities, where $\ast$ denotes a contractible cone:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(g,n)&P_1&P_2&P_3\\\hline
(1,2)&0&\ast&\ast\\
(1,3)&0&1&\ast\\
(2,0)&0&1&\ast\\
(2,1)&0&1&1.
\end{array}                                                    \tag{D.61}
\]
Also $P_3(2,2)$ has exact profinite connectivity one.  Thus both
counterexamples to the proposed connectivity guesses, in D.6 and
D.7, persist in the full and procongruence completions.

There is an exact further comparison in arbitrary genus.  For
$2\leq k\leq6$ and $k<d$, put
\[
c(g,n,k)=
\begin{cases}
k-1,&g=0,\\
\displaystyle\max\left\{k-g,
 \min\left(h(g,n),\left\lfloor\frac{2(k+1)}3\right\rfloor\right)-1
 \right\},&g\geq1.
\end{cases}                                                     \tag{D.62}
\]
For every finite abelian group $A$ and $0\leq j\leq c(g,n,k)$,
the actual Borel and orbit maps induce natural isomorphisms
\[
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_k;A)
       \ \cong\ \varinjlim_{H\triangleleft_f\Gamma_{g,n}}
                         H^j(H;A).                              \tag{D.63}
\]
The maps in the direct limit are restrictions.  Formula (D.63)
identifies the remaining full-level cohomology groups in this
range; it asserts no vanishing of its right side in higher genus.
The procongruence fundamental groups in every rank remain the
exact quotients of D.34.

In particular the complete discrete genus-two answer is:

statement:
The surviving-complex comparison and all genus-two ranks
Put
\[
 \mathcal Y_n=\mathcal C_{2,n}^{\rm lev}
              =\check{\mathcal C}_{2,n}.
\]
Here the curve complex is nonempty, and the equality is the actual
full-to-congruence comparison of D.19.  For $n\geq1$, let $Z_n$
be the full subcomplex of curves that remain essential on forgetting
the last puncture.  Give its completion $Z_n^{\rm lev}$ the levels
induced by $\Gamma_{2,n}$.  Actual forgetting induces, for every
finite constant abelian coefficient group $A$, isomorphisms
\[
 r^*:H^j_{\rm cts}(\mathcal Y_{n-1};A)
       \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\
       H^j_{\rm cts}(Z_n^{\rm lev};A)
       \qquad(j\geq0).                                      \tag{D.69}
\]
For $n=1$ there are no deleted vertices, so
$Z_1^{\rm lev}=\mathcal Y_1$.

For $n\geq2$, let $B_n$ be the profinite set of vertices deleted
by this forgetting: they bound a disk containing the last puncture
and one other puncture.  For every $j\geq2$ there is a natural
isomorphism
\[
 H^j_{\rm cts}(\mathcal Y_n;A)
   \ \cong\
 \frac{C_{\rm cont}\bigl(B_n,
             H^{j-1}_{\rm cts}(\mathcal Y_{n-1};A)\bigr)}
      {H^{j-1}_{\rm cts}(\mathcal Y_{n-1};A)}.                 \tag{D.70}
\]
The denominator is the subgroup of constant functions.
The cohomology group in the target of $C_{\rm cont}$ is given the
discrete topology; these are locally constant functions with finite
image, equivalently the union over finite clopen partitions of
$B_n$.

Set $h_0=2$ and $h_n=n+1$ for $n\geq1$.  Positive-degree
continuous cohomology of $\mathcal Y_n$ with any finite constant
coefficients is zero outside degree $h_n$, and
\[
       H^{h_n}_{\rm cts}(\mathcal Y_n;\mathbb F_2)\ne0 .
                                                               \tag{D.71}
\]
Consequently the full and procongruence completions of every
genus-two rank have exactly the discrete connectivities of D.36:
for $k<d=3+n$, they are $-1,0,1$ at $k=0,1,2$ respectively,
and $k-2$ for $3\leq k<d$.  For $k\geq d$ they are contractible.
Connectivity and exactness have the conventions preceding D.35.

Pointed kernel invariance and upper-rank simple connectivity
For every $g\geq2$ and $n\geq0$, actual puncture forgetting
induces an isomorphism
\[
             K_{g,n+1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_{g,n}.
                                                               \tag{D.85}
\]
For every such genus and every $n\geq0$, the procongruence
level satisfies
\[
             \Pi_1(\check P_k(g,n))=1
                    \qquad\text{for }k\geq3g-2 .
                                                               \tag{D.86}
\]
For $n\geq2$ this includes the noncone ranks
$3g-2\leq k<d$; for $n=0,1$ all displayed ranks
are already cones.  In the noncone range the
cut-kernel map of one explicitly specified
rational-tail multicurve is surjective onto
$K_{g,n}$.  This determines the quotient in D.34
without evaluating that kernel itself.

statement:
Exact discrete connectivity of $P_3(3,0)$
The discrete rank-selected complex $P_3(3,0)$ has exact connectivity
two.  More precisely,
\[
 \pi_1P_3(3,0)=\pi_2P_3(3,0)=0,
 \qquad H_3(P_3(3,0);\mathbb F_2)\ne0.                 \tag{D.89}
\]
The coefficient transport responsible for its second integral
homology has image the entire closed genus-two mapping class group,
and its integral coinvariants vanish.

For its full level completion $Y=P_3(3,0)^{\rm lev}$, the actual
Borel comparison improves (D.63) to
\[
 H^2_{\rm cts}(Y;A)
   \cong\varinjlim_{H\triangleleft_f\Gamma_{3,0}}H^2(H;A)
 \quad\text{for every finite abelian group }A.           \tag{D.90}
\]
Both $Y$ and $\check P_3(3,0)$ have nonzero continuous
$H^3(-;\mathbb F_2)$.  Their fundamental groups are respectively
$1$ and $K_{3,0}$, as in D.11 and D.32.  The right side of (D.90)
and the kernel $K_{3,0}$ are not evaluated by this result.

statement:
All discrete ranks for the closed genus-three surface
The discrete complex $P_4(3,0)$ has exact connectivity two.
The complete closed genus-three discrete table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
 k&0&1&2&3&4&5&k\geq6\\\hline
 \operatorname{conn}P_k(3,0)&-1&0&1&2&2&3&\ast,
\end{array}                                                     \tag{D.97}
\]
where $\ast$ denotes contractibility.  In particular there is
a surjective homomorphism
\[
 H_3(P_4(3,0);\mathbb Z)
   \longrightarrow
 \bigoplus_{(a,b)} H_2(\mathcal C_{2,1}^{\,a,b};\mathbb Z),
                                                               \tag{D.98}
\]
indexed by the exceptional two-curve systems of D.41.
In particular $H_3(P_4(3,0);\mathbb F_2)\ne0$.
At $(g,n,k)=(3,0,4)$ the proposed $(k-1)$-connectivity
would be three, whereas the exact value is two.
The already computed closed lower-genus cases show that this
is the first closed genus in which that proposed bound fails.

For the full level completion of $P_4(3,0)$, the exact
degree-two comparison remains (D.63), and its fundamental group
is trivial.  Its procongruence fundamental group is $K_{3,0}$.
The nonvanishing in (D.98) does not by itself determine continuous
third cohomology of either completion.

The exact third rank in every stable type

previous cases, the complete answer at this rank is
\[
 \operatorname{conn}P_3(g,n)=
 \begin{cases}
 \ast,&3g-3+n\leq3,\\
 1,&g=2,\ n\geq1,\\
 2,&3g-3+n>3,\ g\ne2.
 \end{cases}                                                   \tag{D.100}
\]
For $g\geq3$, both full and procongruence level completions
have nonzero continuous third cohomology with $\mathbb F_2$
coefficients.  For every finite abelian group $A$ the actual
full-level comparison is
\[
 H^2_{\rm cts}(P_3(g,n)^{\rm lev};A)
     \cong\varinjlim_{H\triangleleft_f\Gamma_{g,n}}H^2(H;A).
                                                               \tag{D.101}
\]
Their fundamental groups remain $1$ and $K_{g,n}$,
respectively.  No vanishing of the right side of (D.101)
or of the congruence kernel is asserted.

statement:
The exact fourth rank in every stable type
With $d=3g-3+n$, the discrete rank-four complex has
\[
 \operatorname{conn}P_4(g,n)=
 \begin{cases}
 \ast,&d\leq4,\\
 3,&d>4,\ g=0\text{ or }1,\\
 2,&d>4,\ g\geq2.
 \end{cases}                                                   \tag{D.105}
\]
In every noncone case of genus at least two,
$H_3(P_4(g,n);\mathbb F_2)\ne0$.
For $g\geq3$ there is the actual integral surjection
\[
 H_3(P_4(g,n);\mathbb Z)
   \longrightarrow
 \bigoplus_{\sigma\ \mathrm{exceptional}}
          H_2(\mathcal C(Q_\sigma);\mathbb Z),            \tag{D.106}
\]
with exceptional cores and coefficients as in D.43.
Thus the proposed $(k-1)$-connectivity fails at rank four
in every noncone type of genus at least two.

For genera at most two, the full and procongruence
completions have the same exact values, by D.35 and D.37.
For $g\geq3$, their fundamental groups are $1$ and
$K_{g,n}$ respectively, and full-level degree-two
cohomology is the restriction colimit of (D.63).
The discrete degree-three nonvanishing is not promoted
to a continuous nonvanishing assertion here.

statement:
Complete discrete rank connectivity and the precise completed comparison
Let $(g,n)$ be stable, let $d=3g-3+n$, and let $k\geq0$.
The exact connectivity of the discrete rank-selected complex is
\[
 \operatorname{conn}P_k(g,n)=
 \begin{cases}
 \ast,&k\geq d,\\
 k-1,&0\leq k<d,\quad g=0\text{ or }1,\\
 -1,&k=0,\quad g\geq2,\\
 \lfloor 2k/3\rfloor,&1\leq k\leq3g-4,\quad g\geq2,\\
 k-g,&3g-3\leq k<d,\quad g\geq2.
 \end{cases}                                                   \tag{D.107}
\]
Here $\ast$ denotes contractibility, and exact $-1$ means
nonempty and disconnected.  In every noncone case, if the displayed
integer is $c$, the reduced homology in degree $c+1$ with
$\mathbb F_2$ coefficients is nonzero.

For the full level completion $Y_k=P_k(g,n)^{\rm lev}$, let $c$
be the integer in (D.107).  If $2\leq k\leq6$ and $k<d$, the
actual orbit and Borel maps give, for every finite abelian group
$A$ with constant action,
\[
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_k;A)
       \cong\varinjlim_{H\triangleleft_f\Gamma_{g,n}}H^j(H;A),
                    \qquad 0\leq j\leq c.                     \tag{D.108}
\]
The transition maps are restriction.  In genera at most two,
the full and procongruence completions have the exact values
(D.107), as already proved in D.35 and D.37.  In higher genus,
the right side of (D.108) is not evaluated here; the
procongruence fundamental groups remain the exact kernel
quotients of D.34.  No general higher-genus completed vanishing
is inferred from the discrete formula.

statement:
Actual surviving fibres and higher completed connectivity
Fix $g\geq2$.  Write $Y_{g,n}^{\mathrm f}=\mathcal C_{g,n}^{\rm lev}$
and $Y_{g,n}^{\mathrm c}=\check{\mathcal C}_{g,n}$, and use the
same superscript throughout each displayed formula.
For $n\geq2$, let $Z_{g,n}$ be the subcomplex whose curves remain
essential after forgetting the last puncture.  With the levels
induced by the indicated ambient group, actual forgetting gives
\[
 r^*:H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,n-1}^{\epsilon};A)
       \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
       H^j_{\rm cts}(Z_{g,n}^{\epsilon};A),
 \qquad \epsilon\in\{\mathrm f,\mathrm c\},\quad j\geq0,       \tag{D.116}
\]
for every finite constant abelian coefficient group $A$.
Set $P=\pi_1(S_{g,n-1})$ and let $I_i\leq P$ be the peripheral
cyclic subgroup about the retained puncture $p_i$.
The two deleted-vertex spaces have the common profinite model
\[
 B_{g,n}=\coprod_{i=1}^{n-1}\widehat P/\widehat I_i.
                                                               \tag{D.117}
\]
The natural full-to-congruence map is the identity in these
coordinates.  For a discrete abelian group $M$ put
$R_B(M)=C_{\rm cont}(B,M)/M$, with constants in the denominator.
Then the actual cone and forgetting maps give
\[
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,n}^{\epsilon};A)
       \cong R_{B_{g,n}}\!
          \left(H^{j-1}_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,n-1}^{\epsilon};A)\right),
                     \qquad n\geq2,\quad j\geq2.             \tag{D.118}
\]
The target cohomology in $C_{\rm cont}$ has the discrete topology.
In particular, for $n\geq2$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,n}^{\epsilon};A)&=0
                                  &&(1\leq j\leq n-1),\\
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,n}^{\epsilon};A)
   &\cong R_{B_{g,n}}\cdots R_{B_{g,2}}
          H^{j-n+1}_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,1}^{\epsilon};A)
                                  &&(j\geq n).
\end{aligned}                                                     \tag{D.119}
\]
Under these isomorphisms, the full-to-congruence cohomology
comparison is exactly the iterated $R_B$ applied to the
once-marked comparison.

The full completion $Y_{g,n}^{\mathrm f}$ is at least
$n$-connected for every $n\geq1$.
The procongruence completion $Y_{g,n}^{\mathrm c}$ is at least
$(n-1)$-connected for $n\geq2$.
The groups of the once-marked higher-genus base in (D.119)
are not evaluated.  Thus these are proved lower bounds,
and the displayed recursion retains the exact base modules
and comparison maps.

statement:
Closed cut normalizers and the first-puncture comparison
Let $g\geq2$.  Actual first-puncture forgetting induces
isomorphisms, for every finite constant abelian group $A$,
\[
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,0}^{\epsilon};A)
       \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,1}^{\epsilon};A),
 \qquad j\geq0,\quad\epsilon\in\{\mathrm f,\mathrm c\}.
                                                               \tag{D.124}
\]
The notation is that of D.46.  Consequently its exact
puncture recursion has the closed base
\[
 H^j_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,n}^{\epsilon};A)
   \cong R_{B_{g,n}}\cdots R_{B_{g,2}}\,
           H^{j-n+1}_{\rm cts}(Y_{g,0}^{\epsilon};A),
             \qquad n\geq2,\quad j\geq n.                  \tag{D.125}
\]
The lower-degree vanishing and connectivity bounds of D.46
continue to hold.  The full-to-congruence comparison in
(D.125) is the same iterated functor applied to the closed
comparison.  No higher-genus closed cohomology module,
nor its congruence-kernel quotient fundamental group,
is evaluated here.

and disconnected, and $k\geq d$ remains contractible.

statement:
Puncture invariance and finite central-kernel detection
For $g\geq2$, a finite constant abelian coefficient group $A$, and $j\geq0$, put
\[
 E^j_{g,n}(A)=
 \varinjlim_{H\lhd_f\Gamma_{g,n}}H^j(H;A),                    \tag{D.140}
\]
where the transition maps are restrictions. Actual inflation along puncture
forgetting induces isomorphisms
\[
 E^j_{g,n-1}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}E^j_{g,n}(A)
       \qquad(n\geq1).                                      \tag{D.141}
\]
We have $E^0_{g,n}(A)=A$ and $E^1_{g,n}(A)=0$.

For every finite-index $H\leq\Gamma_{g,0}$ and
$\alpha\in H^2(H;A)$, let
\[
 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E_\alpha
       \xrightarrow{\pi}H\longrightarrow1                  \tag{D.142}
\]
be its central extension. The following four statements are equivalent:
$\alpha$ has zero image in $E^2_{g,0}(A)$; (D.142) splits over a
finite-index subgroup of $H$; some finite quotient of $E_\alpha$ is
injective on $A$; and $E_\alpha$ is residually finite.

The family of these degree-two vanishing questions is equivalently the

 \qquad H\leq_f\Gamma_{g,0}.                                \tag{D.143}

\]

statement:
Finite-index root classes and the remaining homology characters
Let $g\geq3$, $G=\Gamma_{g,0}$, and let
$\chi\in H^2(G;\mathbb Z)$ be the generator normalized so that the
signature class is $4\chi$ and the $p_1$ mapping-cylinder extension
has class $12\chi$. Write $E_{a\chi}$ for the central
$\mathbb Z$-extension with class $a\chi$.
For every $a\in\mathbb Z$ and $N\geq1$, the actual quotient
\[
       E_{a\chi}/N\mathbb Z
       \quad\hbox{is residually finite}.                    \tag{D.146}
\]

For a finite-index $H\leq G$, put
\[
 \begin{split}
 \chi_H&=\operatorname{res}^G_H\chi,\qquad
 \chi_{H,*}:H_2(H;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\\
 \operatorname{im}\chi_{H,*}&=d_H\mathbb Z,\qquad
 K_H=\ker\chi_{H,*}. 
 \end{split}                                                \tag{D.147}
\]
Here $d_H>0$. For every finite constant abelian group $A$, every
$\alpha\in H^2(H;A)$ whose universal-coefficient character
$f_\alpha:H_2(H;\mathbb Z)\to A$ vanishes on $K_H$ restricts to
zero on a finite-index subgroup of $H$. This includes all reductions
of integral classes $\beta$ for which a nonzero multiple is an
integer multiple of $\chi_H$, and also the entire
$\operatorname{Ext}(H_1(H;\mathbb Z),A)$ subgroup.

The exact remaining degree-two obstruction of D.49 is therefore
\[
 E^2_{g,0}(A)\ \cong\
 \varinjlim_{H\lhd_fG}
       \operatorname{Hom}(K_H,A).                           \tag{D.148}
\]
For $H'\leq H$, the transition map on the right is precomposition
with the actual map $K_{H'}\to K_H$ induced by inclusion of groups.
For $A=\mathbb Z/n$, the coefficient Bockstein of a class $\alpha$
is nonzero exactly when $f_\alpha$ is nonzero on
$\operatorname{Tor}H_2(H;\mathbb Z)$. Such torsion characters,
as well as characters on the free part of $K_H$, are retained in the
unevaluated right side of (D.148); no persistence or vanishing of
that colimit is asserted.

The remaining obstruction comes from new finite-index homology
There is an explicit finite central extension
\[
 1\longrightarrow C_2\longrightarrow\widetilde Q
       \longrightarrow Q=\operatorname{Sp}(6,\mathbb F_2)

whose pullback class $\eta\in H^2(\Gamma_{3,0};\mathbb F_2)$
evaluates nontrivially on the order-two abelian cycle of two
disjoint nonseparating twists with connected complement.
It therefore detects the torsion summand of
$H_2(\Gamma_{3,0};\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\oplus C_2$.
The class $\eta$ restricts to zero on the actual mod-two homology
level $\Gamma_{3,0}[2]$.

For every $g\geq3$ and every finite constant abelian $A$, the
initial-group comparison
\[
 H^2_{\rm cts}(\widehat\Gamma_{g,0};A)
       \longrightarrow H^2(\Gamma_{g,0};A)                 \tag{D.158}
\]
is an isomorphism. All these initial-group classes become zero
after a finite-index restriction.
For an arbitrary finite-index $H\leq G=\Gamma_{g,0}$, define
\[
 J_H=\ker\bigl(H_2(H;\mathbb Z)
                    \xrightarrow{i_*}H_2(G;\mathbb Z)\bigr).
\]
The exact residual module of D.50 has the intrinsic form
\[
       E^2_{g,0}(A)\ \cong\
       \varinjlim_{H\lhd_fG}\operatorname{Hom}(J_H,A).
                                                               \tag{D.159}
\]
Its transition maps are precomposition with the actual
inclusion-induced maps $J_{H'}\to J_H$.

is asserted.

statement:
Every finite cyclic group occurs in the Torelli completion kernel
Let $g\geq3$, let $G=\Gamma_{g,0}$, and write
\[
 \rho:G\longrightarrow B=\operatorname{Sp}(2g,\mathbb Z),
 \qquad I=\ker\rho,
 \qquad K_I=\ker(\widehat I\longrightarrow\widehat G).
                                                               \tag{D.163}
\]
For every integer $m\geq2$ there is a continuous epimorphism
\[
                         K_I\longrightarrow C_m.               \tag{D.164}
\]
The maps in this construction are chosen separately for different
$m$. D.53 supplies an additional compatible sequence.

More precisely, there are a normal finite-index subgroup
$H\lhd G$, its actual Torelli intersection $N=H\cap I$, and an
$H$-invariant epimorphism $u:N\to C_m$ such that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 N'=\ker u\lhd H,\qquad [N:N']=m,\qquad
 \overline{N'}^{\,\widehat H}=\overline N^{\,\widehat H},\\
 u(N\cap L)=C_m\quad\text{for every finite-index }L\leq H.
 \end{gathered}                                                \tag{D.165}
\]
In particular, the full profinite topology of $I$ is not the
topology induced by $G$. The nonzero coefficient class
$u\in H^1(N;C_m)$ is fixed by $H/N$ and cannot be killed by any
ambient finite-index refinement. This is an explicit obstruction
to applying the coefficient-killing step of D.49 to the Torelli
sequence. It does not evaluate the colimit (D.159).

statement:
The exact Torelli filtration of the remaining degree-two obstruction
Let $g\geq3$, let $G=\Gamma_{g,0}$, and put
$B=\operatorname{Sp}(2g,\mathbb Z)$, $I=\ker(G\to B)$ and
$K=\ker(\widehat I\to\widehat G)$.
The kernel $K$ is central in $\widehat I$. In particular the maps
$\Phi,j$ of D.53 give an isomorphism of profinite groups
\[
 K\cong\ker(\Phi)\times\widehat{\mathbb Z},
 \qquad (k,t)\longmapsto k\,j(t).                         \tag{D.178}
\]
Fix a finite abelian group $A$, regarded as a constant
coefficient group on every subgroup of $G$ and $B$.
The induced action on fibre cohomology below retains the
conjugation action. For $H\lhd_fG$ set
$N_H=H\cap I$ and $\Lambda_H=\rho(H)$, where $\rho:G\to B$ is
the symplectic representation. Define
\[
 \mathcal E_G^j(A)=\varinjlim_{H\lhd_fG}H^j(H;A),\qquad
 T_A^{p,q}=\varinjlim_{H\lhd_fG}
 H^p\bigl(\Lambda_H;H^q(N_H;A)\bigr).                    \tag{D.179}
\]
The coefficient action in the second formula is the actual
conjugation action from $1\to N_H\to H\to\Lambda_H\to1$.
All transition maps are restriction on the base followed by
restriction on the fibre coefficient. There is a natural
first-quadrant spectral sequence
\[
 T_A^{p,q}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal E_G^{p+q}(A),
 \qquad d_r:E_r^{p,q}\longrightarrow E_r^{p+r,q-r+1},
 \qquad E_2^{p,q}=T_A^{p,q}.                              \tag{D.180}
\]
Writing $\mathcal E_B^p(A)$ for the corresponding restriction
colimit over normal finite-index subgroups of $B$, its bottom
row and two other terms are
\[
 T_A^{p,0}=\mathcal E_B^p(A),\qquad
 T_A^{0,1}\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A),\qquad
 T_A^{1,1}=0.                                            \tag{D.181}
\]
The first differential induces an injection
\[
 \theta_A=d_2:\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A)
                   \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
                         \mathcal E_B^2(A).              \tag{D.182}
\]
Define the two groups and their actual differentials by
\[
 \begin{split}
 U_A&=\ker\bigl(d_2:T_A^{0,2}\longrightarrow T_A^{2,1}\bigr),\\
 P_A&=\ker\bigl(d_3:U_A\longrightarrow\mathcal E_B^3(A)\bigr).
 \end{split}                                             \tag{D.183}
\]
Here $U_A=E_3^{0,2}$ and the stated target of $d_3$ is exactly
$E_3^{3,0}$, rather than a further unspecified quotient.
There is a natural short exact sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow
 \frac{\mathcal E_B^2(A)}{\theta_A\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,A)}
 \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{inf}\ }
 \mathcal E_G^2(A)
 \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{res}\ }P_A
 \longrightarrow0.                                      \tag{D.184}
\]
Together with D.51, its middle term is canonically
$\varinjlim_{H\lhd_fG}\operatorname{Hom}(J_H,A)$, where
$J_H=\ker[H_2(H;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(G;\mathbb Z)]$ and the
transition maps are precomposition with the actual inclusion
maps on $H_2$. Neither outer term of (D.184) is evaluated here.

statement:
The strict completion and its finite representations
For every stable $(g,n)$, set
\[
 \widehat C_{g,n}=\varprojlim_R C_{g,n}/R,
\]
where $R$ ranges over finite-index congruences on all Hom-sets, with the
object set fixed.  Composition makes this a category internal to
profinite sets, and restriction along $C_{g,n}\longrightarrow\widehat
C_{g,n}$ is an equivalence
\[
 \operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{cts}}(\widehat C_{g,n},\mathrm{FinSet})
       \simeq \operatorname{Fun}(C_{g,n},\mathrm{FinSet}).       \tag{E.1}
\]
Every functor between two such finite-object categories extends to their
strict completions.  A natural transformation extends as well, and the
extensions preserve its equations.

statement:
Constructible finite coefficients in every stable type
Fix $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$.  For every stable
$(g,n)$ there are equivalences, compatible with stalk functors,
\[
 \operatorname{Cons}_{\partial,\mathrm{fin}}
       ((\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})_{\overline{\mathbb Q},\mathrm{et}})
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Cons}_{\partial,\mathrm{fin}}
       ((\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})^{\mathrm{an}})
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{cts}}(\widehat C_{g,n},\mathrm{FinSet}).
                                                               \tag{E.2}
\]
Here $\operatorname{Cons}_{\partial,\mathrm{fin}}$ means finite-stalk
sheaves locally constant on every topological-type stratum of the fixed
boundary stratification.  Jansen, Corollary 6.6 and Theorem 6.7, and
Barwick--Glasman--Haine, Proposition 12.6.4, give the inputs.

Primitive meridians and retracts at all five-point flags

\[
 G,\quad F_2,\quad \mathbb Z\times F_2,\quad

\]
All these groups are good, and the finite categorical quotients induce

statement:
The kernel for an automorphism of an extension
Let $1\to K\to E\to Q\to1$ be an exact sequence of finitely generated
profinite groups, with $Z(K)=Z(Q)=1$, and let
$\rho:Q\to\operatorname{Out}(K)$ be its outer monodromy.  Restriction
and passage to the quotient give an isomorphism
\[
 \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Out}(E;K)\longrightarrow
                    \operatorname{Out}(Q)\bigr)
       \simeq C_{\operatorname{Out}(K)}(\rho(Q)).             \tag{E.8}
\]
The same formula holds after imposing any invariant peripheral
condition on the restriction to $K$, by intersecting the right side
with the corresponding subgroup of $\operatorname{Out}(K)$.

statement:
An explicit inertia-preserving GT lift to

Put $K=\widehat\pi_{1,2}$, $Q=\widehat\Gamma_{1,2}$ and
$E=\widehat\Gamma_{1,3}$, where all marks are ordered and the
map $E\to Q$ forgets the third mark.  The standard GT action on
$\widehat B_5$ induces a continuous homomorphism
\[
 \Psi:\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\longrightarrow
           \operatorname{Out}(E;K)
                                                               \tag{E.10}
\]
whose quotient action on $Q=\widehat B_4/Z(\widehat B_4)$ is the
standard action of Minamide--Nakamura, Theorem~4.3(i).  Its restriction
to $K$ fixes both cusp classes with the common multiplier $\lambda$,

$\operatorname{Out}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,3})$ preserving the kernel

two peripheral subgroup conjugacy classes.  Then
\[
 A_{\rm per}=\langle\delta\rangle\times

       \simeq C_2\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}},          \tag{E.14}
\]
where $\delta$ interchanges the two original labels.  Every element
has one common peripheral exponent, normalizes $\langle\delta\rangle$,
and preserves nonseparating twist inertia.  Thus the group $A$ and
its subgroup $A^I$ in LM3b E.1/E.9 coincide, and
$A/\mathfrak S_2\simeq\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$.

statement:
The two elliptic boundary maps and forgetting
Put $G_2=\widehat B_4/\langle\omega _4\rangle$ and
$G_1=\widehat B_3/\langle\omega _3^2\rangle$, where
$\omega _r=(\sigma _1\cdots\sigma _{r-1})^r$ and brackets on
central profinite subgroups mean closed subgroups.  Under the
geometric identifications $G_i=\widehat\Gamma_{1,i}$, forgetting
the second mark is
\[
 q:G_2\longrightarrow G_1,\qquad
 (\sigma _1,\sigma _2,\sigma _3)\longmapsto(a,b,a),
 \quad a=\sigma _1,\ b=\sigma _2\text{ in }G_1.       \tag{E.16}
\]
The rational-tail boundary has stabilizer $\widehat B_3\subset G_2$,
twist $\omega _3^2$, and normalization group $G_1$.
For the nonseparating twist $a=\sigma _1\in G_2$, put
$v=\sigma _2\sigma _1^2\sigma _2$ and $d=\sigma _3$.
Its stabilizer $H_a$ is generated by $a,v,d$ and satisfies
\[
 [a,v]=[a,d]=1,\qquad (vd)^2=(dv)^2,\qquad
                    a^2(vd)^2=1.                         \tag{E.17}
\]
Consequently
\[
 H_a/\langle a\rangle\simeq
 \widehat A_3/\langle\omega _3\rangle,
 \quad A_3=\langle\sigma _1^2,\sigma _2\rangle\subset B_3,
                                                               \tag{E.18}
\]
with $\sigma _1^2\mapsto v$ and $\sigma _2\mapsto d$.
This is the fundamental group of
$\mathcal M_{0,\{1,2\},[+,-]}$, the four-point normalization
with its two node branches unordered.  Its geometric branch
character is $v\mapsto1$, $d\mapsto0$ in $C_2$.
For every
$F=(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$, the genuine
braid actions commute with (E.16), with the rational-tail
quotient, and with (E.18), including its branch permutation.

statement:
The orbifold normalizer maps and their parameter
For $r=3,4$, put $F_r=\widehat F(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ with its
$r+1$ peripheral classes, $D_r=F_r/\overline{\langle\!\langle
x_1^2,\ldots,x_r^2\rangle\!\rangle}$, and
$K_r=\ker(D_r\to C_2)$, every $x_i$ mapping to the
nonidentity element.  Then $K_3=\widehat\pi_{1,1}$ and
$K_4=\widehat\pi_{1,2}$.  Let $\mathcal A_r$ be the genuine
peripheral automorphism group fixing the infinity class, and
$\widetilde N_r$ the inverse image in $\mathcal A_r$ of the
normalizer of the full geometric sphere group
$\Sigma_{0,r+1}\subset\operatorname{Out}_{\rm lac}(F_r)$.
Quotient-and-restriction
\[

statement:
Cote 143 uses geometric base change, and individual faithfulness
\label{sec:E-manuscript}
In cote 143, scans 29--33, the group denoted
$\widehat\Gamma_{g,n}=\pi_1(\overline M_{g,n})$ is the
geometric fundamental group of the \emph{open} moduli stack:
the bar in this passage denotes base change to
$\overline{\mathbb Q}$.  Its arithmetic action is
\[
 G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow
             \operatorname{Out}(\widehat P\Gamma_{g,n}).        \tag{E.30}
\]
For every stable type of positive modular dimension this
homomorphism is injective, as is its procongruence quotient
action.  For $(0,3)$ it is the trivial homomorphism to $1$.
With the usual pure mapping class groups in the unstable
cases, it is trivial for $(0,0),(0,1),(0,2)$ and faithful
for $(1,0)$.

The surface group $\widehat\pi_{0,3}=\widehat F_2$ occurring
in scans 29--30 is instead the kernel of the next universal
curve sequence.  More precisely
\[
 \widehat\pi_{0,3}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \widehat P\Gamma_{0,4},\qquad
 \widehat P\Gamma_{0,3}=1.                                    \tag{E.31}
\]
Thus the tripod automorphism assertion and the four-point
modular-group assertion are related by this specified
isomorphism; they are not two assertions about the trivial
three-point modular group.

statement:
The exact involution and centralizer fibres of LM6 C.15
Let $P^{\pm}=P\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle$ be a profinite
group with $\tau^2=1$, let $K$ be a closed normal
$\tau$-stable subgroup of $P$, and put $Q=P/K$.
Write $\alpha(k)=\tau k\tau^{-1}$.  The compact pointed set
\[
 H^1(C_2,K)=
 \{k\in K:k\alpha(k)=1\}/
       (k\sim b k\alpha(b)^{-1},\ b\in K)
\]
has an action of $C_Q(\bar\tau)$ given by
\[
 q(g)\cdot[k]=[g k\alpha(g)^{-1}],\qquad g\in P.               \tag{E.38}
\]
The $P$-conjugacy classes of involutions of $P^{\pm}$ whose
images are $Q$-conjugate to $\bar\tau$ are exactly
\[
 C_Q(\bar\tau)\backslash H^1(C_2,K).                           \tag{E.39}
\]
For each cocycle $k$ there is an exact sequence of profinite
groups
\[
 1\longrightarrow K^{k\tau}\longrightarrow C_P(k\tau)
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Stab}_{C_Q(\bar\tau)}([k])
 \longrightarrow1.                                           \tag{E.40}
\]
In particular the quotient centralizer need not fix the
trivial class, and the entire set $H^1$ cannot generally
replace its orbit set in (E.39).

\]

$x\mapsto1,y\mapsto0$.  Write $c_2(f)$ for the exponent

 f(d,v^2)d^{-4c_2(f)}f(v,d^2)=v^{4c_2(f)}\quad\hbox{in }R.

statement:
The arithmetic image, with exact indices and witness tests
For the geometric modular groups in cote 143, let
$A_{g,n}$ be the subgroup of their outer automorphisms
preserving the boundary-inertia conjugacy classes and
centralizing the specified relabelling action.  In genus

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 n& A_{0,n}&\rho_{0,n}:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow A_{0,n}\\\hline
 0,1,2,3&1&\text{trivial}\\
 4&\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}_0&\text{the tripod action}\\
 n\geq5&\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}&\text{the standard inclusion}.
\end{array}                                                     \tag{E.56}
\]
The surface-tripod formulation occurs at surface type
$(0,3)$ through
$\widehat\pi_{0,3}\simeq\widehat\Gamma_{0,4}$.

unresolved equality $G_{\mathbb Q}=\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$.
The same equality describes the arithmetic image in
$\operatorname{Out}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,2})$, whose group
is GT and whose boundary inertia is preserved by E.11.
The remaining individual positive-genus targets are not
classified by the results of this section; E.17 establishes
their arithmetic faithfulness in its stated range. For the
ordinary full labelled exit system classified by E.42,
arithmetic surjectivity is again exactly the equality
$G_{\mathbb Q}=\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$.

For the full gentle element independently constructed
in E.46 with the exact frames designated in LM7 E.58, the tests for

multiplier one and trivial peripheral homology all pass.

statement:
The diagonal stabilizer has the full profinite topology
Fix a stable labelled surface, its mapping class group $\Gamma$, and a
multicurve $\sigma$.  Put
\[
 C=\Stab_\Gamma(\sigma),\qquad
 \Delta=\langle\tau_c:c\in\sigma\rangle,\qquad H=C/\Delta.
\]
In the completed transporter exit category of A.4 and E.1, the
automorphism groups of the open and $\sigma$ objects are
$\widehat\Gamma$ and $\widehat H$, and
\[
 \Hom(\sigma,\varnothing)=\widehat\Gamma/\widehat\Delta.
                                                               \tag{E.79}
\]
The automorphism group of the distinguished crossing arrow, with
\emph{both} endpoints allowed to vary, is canonically
\[
 \widehat C\ \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\
       \widehat\Gamma\times\widehat H,
 \qquad c\longmapsto(c,\bar c).                                \tag{E.80}
\]
This is an embedding of the full profinite completion of $C$.
For the multicurve obtained by attaching a labelled three-holed
sphere to each boundary of a stable bordered surface, (E.80)
recovers the full completion of its boundary-fixed mapping class
group, including every boundary twist.

All-genus tripod normalizers and their crossing maps
Start with a stable surface of type $(g,n)$, choose distinct
marked points $p_1,\ldots,p_r$, and replace each by a labelled
pair $(p_i,x_i)$ on an attached three-pointed rational tail.
Let $\sigma$ be the resulting multicurve on the surface of
type $(g,n+r)$, $\Gamma$ its pure mapping class group,
$C=\Stab_\Gamma(\sigma)$, and
$\Delta=\langle\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_r\rangle$ its twist lattice.
Then
\[
 \widehat C\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\widehat\Gamma,
 \qquad
 N_{\widehat\Gamma}(\widehat\Delta)
   =C_{\widehat\Gamma}(\widehat\Delta)=\widehat C.             \tag{E.100}
\]
In particular the right action of
$\widehat{C/\Delta}$ on the completed crossing
$\widehat\Gamma/\widehat\Delta$ is faithful and free.

Fix this collection of tails and take the full subcategory
whose objects are the open stratum and the strata associated
to its subsets.  A continuous autoequivalence fixing these
objects is determined, up to natural isomorphism, by its
outer action on $\widehat\Gamma$.  The comparison includes
all its crossing maps, and uses the full completions in every
genus.  For $r=n$ its deepest crossing recovers the fully
boundary-fixed group $\widehat\Gamma_{g,n}^{\partial}$.

\[

 \qquad \eta_i:A_i\longrightarrow B_i.                       \tag{E.160}
\]

exit category, the space of commutative squares from $\eta_0$ to

the full completion of the bordered-core transporter
\[
 \operatorname{Trans}_{\Stab(t)}(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)
                         /\Delta_{\gamma_0}.                 \tag{E.161}

\[
 (\widehat C_1\times\widehat C_0)/\widehat S,
 \quad C_i=\Stab(t,\gamma_i)/\Delta_{\gamma_i},\quad
 S=\Stab(t,\gamma_0,\gamma_1)/\Delta_{\gamma_1}.               \tag{E.162}
\]

are dense in this actual completed square space.

profinite topology of $G$, has its full induced topology, and
\[
 N_{\widehat G}(\widehat\Delta_\sigma)
 =C_{\widehat G}(\widehat\Delta_\sigma)
 =\widehat C_\sigma.                                         \tag{E.170}
\]
For the entire genus-zero exit category, the finite ambient
transporter quotients $C_N$ below, with $N$ ranging over all
finite-index normal subgroups of $G$, are cofinal among all

crossing from a target stratum to the open stratum consequently

in E.16, for every $n$, independently of a procongruence curve

The compatible-pair group is the graph of the elliptic involution

$A=(\lambda,f_A)$, $B=(\lambda,f_B)$ in $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$

\[
 f_B(u^2,w^2)=w^{2a}f_A(u,w^4)u^{2b}(uw^2)^{2k}
                   \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3.             \tag{E.200}
\]

\[
 I\Gamma=\{(A,\mathcal J(A)):A\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\},
 \qquad \operatorname{pr}_0:I\Gamma

boundary stratum, let $X$ be its Bers bordification, and put
$G=\check\Gamma$.  Let $N\triangleleft_oG$ range over open
normal subgroups and set $\Gamma_N=\Gamma\cap N$.
There is a natural map of sets
\[
 \Phi:(X\times G)/\Gamma\longrightarrow
                 \varprojlim_N X/\Gamma_N,
 \qquad
 \Phi_N([x,g])=[\gamma_N^{-1}x],
 \quad \gamma_N\equiv g\pmod N.                 \tag{E.248}
\]
The action in the source is the diagonal left action.
This map is not injective.  In particular, the natural
isomorphism with this diagonal quotient asserted in the
proof of Boggi's Theorem~6.3, PDF p.~29,
\cite{ET_Boggi2014} is false as a statement about these
underlying sets.

For a fixed boundary point $p\in X$, write
$S=\operatorname{Stab}_\Gamma(p)$.  The exact replacement
on its orbit is
\[
 \Gamma\backslash((\Gamma p)\times G)
       \cong G/S
       \longrightarrow G/\overline S
       \xrightarrow{\sim}
           \varprojlim_N\Gamma_N\backslash\Gamma/S.
                                                               \tag{E.249}
\]
Here the middle map is the actual quotient map and
$\overline S$ is closure in $G$.  Formula (E.249) is a
statement about the fixed orbit and its finite-level
completion.  No global corrected Bers model is asserted.

statement:
Commuting twists give mutual ellipticity of the cut splittings
Let $S=S_{g,n}$ be hyperbolic, let
$\Pi=\pi_1(S)$, and let $\alpha,\beta$ be profinite geometric
curves.  Write $t_\alpha,t_\beta\in\check\Gamma_{g,n}$ for
their primitive positive twists.  Suppose that
$[t_\alpha,t_\beta]=1$.
For an actual curve $\alpha$, let $S_v$ be the components
obtained by cutting along it and let $H_v=\pi_1(S_v)\leq\Pi$,
with the embeddings specified by paths to the base point.
Every oriented generator $b$ representing $\beta$ satisfies
\[
 b\in x\widehat H_vx^{-1}
       \quad\hbox{for some }v\hbox{ and }x\in\widehat\Pi .
                                                               \tag{E.270}
\]
For a profinite $\alpha$, transport these cut groups by an
element of $\check\Gamma_{g,n}$ carrying an actual curve
to $\alpha$; the conclusion is independent of that
choice, up to the indicated conjugacies and component
permutations.  Equivalently, the cyclic group of each
curve fixes a vertex in the other's completed surface
cut tree.  Thus the two one-edge splittings are mutually
elliptic.

This is a statement about the actual maps from completed
cut-component groups to $\widehat\Pi$.  The remaining
step in E.45 is whether the globally profinite geometric
curve in (E.270) lies in the completed geometric link,
or equals $\alpha$.  The assertion proved here does not
identify that intersection of curve loci.

statement:
The support of a twist commuting with a full pants multitwist
Let $S=S_{g,n}$ be stable with $d=3g-3+n>0$, and put
$G=\check\Gamma_{g,[n]}$; the same statements hold in its pure subgroup.
Let $P$ be an actual simplex of its procongruence curve complex with
$d$ vertices.  Choose positive integers $m_\gamma$, for $\gamma\in P$,
and $\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$, and set
\[
 D_P=\prod_{\gamma\in P}t_\gamma^{\lambda m_\gamma},\qquad
 \mathcal T_{\rm op}(S)=
 \{t_\beta^h:\ \beta\in\check C(S)^0,
                 \ h\widehat{\mathbb Z}\text{ is open in }
                    \widehat{\mathbb Z}\}.
                                                        \tag{E.290}
\]
Here the power condition means exactly $h=a u$ with
$a\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and
$u\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}$.
Then the following equality holds in the actual ambient group:
\[
 C_G(D_P)\cap\mathcal T_{\rm op}(S)
       =\bigcup_{\gamma\in P}
          \{t_\gamma^h:h\widehat{\mathbb Z}
                              \text{ is open}\}.
                                                        \tag{E.291}
\]
In particular a primitive geometric twist commutes with $D_P$
exactly when its curve is a vertex of $P$.

The complete centralizer, including its finite graph action, is
\[
 C_G(D_P)=
 \{g\in\operatorname{Stab}_G(P):
          m_{g\gamma}=m_\gamma\text{ for every }\gamma\in P\}.
                                                        \tag{E.292}
\]
If $P$ is discrete, this is the closure of the discrete centralizer
of $\prod_{\gamma\in P}t_\gamma^{m_\gamma}$.
Writing $\mathfrak A(P,m)$ for automorphisms of the trivalent half-edge dual
graph preserving the edge weights and the permitted external-label
action, its exact cut sequence is
\[
 1\longrightarrow\Delta_P
 \longrightarrow C_G(D_P)
 \longrightarrow\mathfrak A(P,m)
 \longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \Delta_P=\prod_{\gamma\in P}\widehat{\mathbb Z}\,t_\gamma .
                                                        \tag{E.293}
\]
For the pure group every external label is fixed; for the displayed
mixed group external labels may be permuted.  No splitting of
this finite extension is claimed.
