statement:
The relative fixed-point comparison and a finite two-edge refinement
Let $S$ be a hyperbolic oriented surface and put
$\Pi=\widehat{\pi_1(S)}$.  Let $\alpha\ne\beta$ be profinite
geometric curves with commuting primitive twists in
$\check\Gamma(S)$.  Write $T_\alpha,T_\beta$ for their actual
completed cut trees, and $C_\alpha,C_\beta\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}$
for the specified edge groups, with the chosen conjugacy pins.
There is a profinite $\Pi$-tree $R$ with a finite quotient having
exactly two edge orbits and continuous equivariant collapse maps
\[
 T_\alpha\ \xleftarrow{\ q_\alpha\ }\ R
       \ \xrightarrow{\ q_\beta\ }\ T_\beta .
                                                        \tag{E.300}
\]
The map $q_\alpha$ collapses precisely the $\beta$-edge subtrees;
$q_\beta$ collapses precisely the $\alpha$-edge subtrees.
The retained edge groups and their inclusions in $\Pi$ are the
given $C_\alpha,C_\beta$.  In particular the comparison preserves
the actual ambient markings of the two one-edge splittings.

More precisely, after making $\alpha$ discrete by its geometric
procongruence transport, $C_\beta$ fixes a unique vertex of
$T_\alpha$.  Its stabilizer $H$ is the completed fundamental group
of the corresponding actual cut component.  The $H$-action on
$T_\beta$ contains a closed invariant subtree $D_0$ with exactly
one edge orbit $H/C_\beta$ and with no fixed vertex.  Thus
$H\backslash D_0$ is a segment or a loop, with its actual
stabilizer inclusions, and $R$ is the blowup of the carrier
vertices by $D_0$.

The construction proves the finite graph-of-profinite-groups
comparison (E.300).  Identifying its new vertex pairs with marked
surface pairs and with the configuration specialization of a
two-node PSC degeneration remains the explicit geometric step
in E.45; no such identification is included in this result.

statement:
Every finite commuting geometric family has a canonical finite refinement
Let $\Sigma=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m\}$ be a finite nonempty
family of distinct profinite geometric curves on a hyperbolic
oriented surface $S$.  Suppose their primitive twists commute
pairwise in $\check\Gamma(S)$.  Put $\Pi=\widehat{\pi_1(S)}$.
Choose the actual cut trees $T_i$ and pins for their cyclic
edge groups $C_i\subset\Pi$, so $E(T_i)=\Pi/C_i$.

There is a specified simply connected profinite $\Pi$-graph
$R_\Sigma$, with exactly $m$ edge orbits and at most $2m$
vertex orbits, and actual equivariant collapse maps
\[
 q_i:R_\Sigma\longrightarrow T_i,\qquad
 E(R_\Sigma)=\coprod_{i=1}^m\Pi/C_i .                   \tag{E.310}
\]
The map $q_i$ retains exactly the $i$th edge space, by the
identity on $\Pi/C_i$, and collapses all other edge spaces.
The joint map on vertices is injective.  Every vertex group
is the actual intersection
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}_\Pi(v)
    =\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Stab}_\Pi(q_i(v)).     \tag{E.311}
\]
The finite graph of stabilizers has proper fundamental group
equal to $\Pi$, by these actual inclusion maps and transport
elements.  Every incident edge inclusion is proper; in particular
this finite graph of groups is reduced.

For every nonempty subfamily $\Sigma'\subset\Sigma$ there is
a specified collapse $q_{\Sigma,\Sigma'}$ retaining precisely
its edge colors.  These maps satisfy the literal equalities
\[
 q_{\Sigma',\Sigma''}\,q_{\Sigma,\Sigma'}
       =q_{\Sigma,\Sigma''},\qquad
 q_{\Sigma,\Sigma}=\operatorname{id},                  \tag{E.312}
\]
for nonempty nested subfamilies.  The construction and all these
maps are independent of the order of refinement, through the
explicit common model below.  In particular it applies to the
image of a full pants family of nonseparating curves under an
$I_0$-preserving automorphism of the individual procongruence
group in E.45.

This result constructs the finite simultaneous graph and its
ambient group marking.  The surface-pair and configuration
markings of its new vertices remain the comparison specified
in E.45 and E.52.

statement:
A counterexample to unrestricted induction reflection
Let $k=\mathbb F_3$.  There are a profinite metabelian group
$G$, a closed normal subgroup $H$, and a compact continuous
$k[[H]]$-module $M$ such that
\[
 d_{k[[H]]}(M)=\infty,
 \qquad
 d_{k[[G]]}\bigl(k[[G]]\widehat\otimes_{k[[H]]}M\bigr)=1.
                                                        \tag{E.330}
\]
Here generators are topological module generators, and the
tensor product is the completed tensor product in the category
of compact continuous modules.  The ambient group can be chosen
two-generated.  The counterexample then pulls back along an
actual epimorphism from the free profinite group of rank two,
and along the explicit rank-two free quotients of every
hyperbolic surface completion.

Consequently the unrestricted assertion that completed
induction reflects finite generation, stated in the introduction
of Corob Cook--Vannacci, is false.  The example also disproves
property FIM, at the prime $3$, for the just specified free and
surface groups in the sense of Wilkes' Definition~1.29.
It does not decide the finiteness of the particular vertex pairs
constructed in E.52--E.53; their specific finiteness conditions
still require proof.

statement:
Cofinal covers give proper pro-$p$ surface-pair image graphs
Let $S=S_{g,n}$ with $g\geq3$, let
$\Pi=\widehat{\pi_1(S)}$, and let
$\Sigma=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m\}$, $m>1$, be distinct
nonseparating profinite geometric curves whose primitive twists
commute pairwise.  Let $R=R_\Sigma$ be the specified E.53
refinement, with its actual edge and vertex stabilizers.
For every open subgroup $U\leq\Pi$ and every finite set
$\mathcal P$ of primes there is a characteristic open subgroup
$K\leq U$ with the following properties, simultaneously for
$p\in\mathcal P$.

Choose the finite graph-of-groups presentation supplied by the
$K$-action on $R$.  Write $A_w$ for its vertex groups, $C_e$
for its edge groups, and $t_e$ for its chosen transport elements.
Let $K^{(p)}$ denote the maximal pro-$p$ quotient of $K$ and set
\[
 B_{w,p}=\operatorname{im}(A_w\longrightarrow K^{(p)}),
 \qquad
 D_{e,p}=\operatorname{im}(C_e\longrightarrow K^{(p)}).
                                                        \tag{E.350}
\]
The finite graph of these actual image groups, with the images
of the incidence maps and $t_e$, is proper and reduced, and
its pro-$p$ fundamental group is the specified $K^{(p)}$.
Every $D_{e,p}$ is $\mathbb Z_p$ and every $B_{w,p}$ is
noncyclic.  Assign each original cusp of the finite covering
surface $S_K$ to its unique fixed vertex of $R$.
Then each $B_{w,p}$, with its incident edge groups and assigned
cusp groups, is an orientable pro-$p$ $PD^2$ pair.  In particular
it has an actual finite standard surface-pair basis.
There is a peripheral-preserving automorphism of $K^{(p)}$
identifying this graph splitting with a geometric multicurve
splitting of $S_K$.

These assertions remain true after passing from $K$ to any
further open subgroup.  Thus the construction gives a cofinal
family of characteristic covers, simultaneously for every
prescribed finite prime set.  The comparison from the original
full graph to its pro-$p$ image graph is the actual coset map
specified below.  The proof here constructs the images
$B_{w,p}$.  E.56 proves that every canonical map
$A_w^{(p)}\twoheadrightarrow B_{w,p}$ is an isomorphism.
The full profinite vertex-pair and compatible
PFC-admissible configuration marking remain to be supplied.

Actual virtually pro-$p$ quotients and all finite-coefficient dualities
Fix a prime $p$ and a vertex group $H$ in one of the
covering graphs of E.56.  Let $\mathcal S=(S_1,\ldots,S_b)$
be its specified nonempty family of incident edge and
original cusp subgroups.  Each $S_i$ is the actual
infinite procyclic subgroup with its fixed local flag.
For every finite continuous $p$-primary $H$-module $M$
there is an actual quotient map of pairs
\[
 (H,\mathcal S)\longrightarrow (G,\mathcal T)             \tag{E.390}
\]
through which the action on $M$ factors, such that
$G$ is virtually free pro-$p$, is $p$-torsion-free,
and $(G,\mathcal T)$ is an orientable $PD^2$ pair
at $p$ in the finite-projective-resolution sense of
\cite{ET_WilkesRelative2017}.
Inflation along (E.390) identifies the absolute and
relative cohomology with coefficients in every finite
$p$-primary $G$-module with that of its pullback to $H$.

There is a compatible trace
\[
 \operatorname{tr}_H:
 H^2(H,\mathcal S;\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p)
             \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p   \tag{E.391}
\]
normalized by any one specified outward boundary
generator.  Put $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}
(M,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p)$, with its contragredient
$H$-action.  Cup product and evaluation give perfect
pairings of finite groups
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H^i(H,M)\times H^{2-i}(H,\mathcal S;M^\vee)
       &\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p,\\
 H^i(H,\mathcal S;M)\times H^{2-i}(H,M^\vee)
       &\longrightarrow\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p
 \end{aligned}
 \qquad(0\leq i\leq2).                                  \tag{E.392}
\]
The pairings use the intrinsic trace (E.391), so they
do not depend on the choice of quotient (E.390).
They are natural in the finite coefficient module.
The same assertions hold for every open subgroup
$H_1\leq H$ with its actual induced peripheral family.
Restriction, corestriction and the traces have their
usual finite-cover compatibility, proved below by
the actual boundary maps.

type $p$-$\mathrm{FP}_\infty$, or that its full
profinite marking is geometric, is included here.

statement:
A directed family of proper finite-edge fillings with finitely presented vertices
Let $\Pi$ and $R_\Sigma$ be the full surface completion and the
finite simultaneous refinement of E.53. Fix the actual finite
graph of groups $Y=\Pi\backslash R_\Sigma$, vertex representatives
$A_v$, edge groups $C_e\cong\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, incidence
inclusions, and transport elements $t_e$. The original cusp
subgroups at each vertex retain their individual labels.
For every $N\triangleleft_o\Pi$ there is an actual quotient graph
of profinite groups with finite cyclic edges and with fundamental
group
\[
 \Pi_N=\Pi/\overline{\langle\!\langle
          C_e^{\,n_e(N)}:e\in EY\rangle\!\rangle},
 \qquad n_e(N)=|\operatorname{im}(C_e\to\Pi/N)|.          \tag{E.410}
\]
Every edge has exactly the displayed order. The quotient graph
is proper, and every one of its full profinite vertex groups is
topologically finitely presented. For $N'\subseteq N$, the
quotient maps on vertices, edges, transports and cusp flags
form a literal morphism of graphs of groups, and these morphisms
compose as the corresponding inclusions of $N$'s do.

The original groups and all their flag maps are recovered by
these specified inverse limits:
\[
 \Pi\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_N\Pi_N,
 \qquad A_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_N A_v(N),
 \qquad C_e\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_N
                         C_e/C_e^{n_e(N)}.              \tag{E.411}
\]
The same assertion holds for each original cusp subgroup,
using its actual image at each stage.
For the all-nonseparating family used in E.45, all these
conclusions hold for the common-exponent quotients
\[
 \Pi^{[r]}=\Pi/\overline{\langle\!\langle
                   C_e^r:e\in EY\rangle\!\rangle},
 \qquad r_k=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,k),             \tag{E.425}
\]
with exactly order-$r$ edges for every positive integer $r$.
The sequence $r_k$ recovers the same original groups and flags.
The finite-generation bounds proved below depend on $|\Pi/N|$.
No uniform vertex-generator bound or identification of the
filled vertices as Fuchsian groups is asserted.

All-prime strong duality and surface pro-$p$ quotients do not determine the full surface completion
Let $g\geq2$, let $\Pi_g$ be the discrete closed orientable

 D_p=\Pi_g^{(p)},\qquad G_g=\prod_pD_p.

\[

                                                               \tag{E.451}
\]

topologically finitely presented in the full profinite category.
For every prime $p$, its projection to $D_p$ is its own maximal

make (E.451) an isomorphism. This example does not supply the

 \begin{aligned}

       &\xrightarrow{\sim}D^{\mathrm{ab},p},\\
       bC_i&\longmapsto
          \bigl[\widetilde b\,s_i^{r_i}\widetilde b^{-1}\bigr].

\]

quotient of $D$, and $\widetilde b$ is any lift in $H$.

 e_{i,x}&\longmapsto[xs_i^{r_i}x^{-1}].

\]
Every basis member is the primitive generator of the

An explicit group for the four-point unringed topos
Choose a geometric generic point of $\mathbf P^1_k$.  For each finite
set $B\subset\mathbf P^1(k)$ of size at least three let
$F_B=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathbf P^1_k-B)$, with the filling maps
$F_{B'}\twoheadrightarrow F_B$ for $B\subset B'$.  Thus $F_B$ is free
profinite of rank $|B|-1$, with its specified peripheral procyclic
subgroups.  Put
\[
 G=\varprojlim_B F_B.
\]
For each $x\in U(k)$ let $[I_x]$ be the compatible conjugacy class of
inertia above $x$, a copy of $\widehat\Z(1)$ in $G$.  Then generic
restriction gives an isomorphism
\[
 \Aut(U_{\mathrm{et}})\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\
 \bigl\{[\alpha]\in\Out_{\mathrm{cont}}(G):
   \alpha\text{ permutes }\{[I_x]:x\in U(k)\}\bigr\}.
 \tag{E.T2}
\]
The group on the right is specified by the inverse system of free
profinite groups and filling maps just given.  Every automorphism in
it has a unique induced permutation of $U(k)$.  Moreover
$N_G(I_x)=I_x$, and generic restriction has trivial kernel.

statement:
Relative reconstruction from all modular sheaves
Fix $k=\overline\Q$ and a universe of $k$-schemes.  Put
$\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sh}((\operatorname{Sch}/k)_{\rm et})$.
For the algebraic moduli stack $\mathcal X=\mathcal M_{g,n,k}$,
including the four unstable types, let $\mathcal C_{\mathcal X}$
have objects $(T,x)$ with $x\in\mathcal X(T)$, morphisms
$(f,\alpha):(T,x)\to(T',x')$ with
$\alpha:x\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*x'$, and coverings induced by
etale covering families of $T$.  Retain the projection
\[
 p_{\mathcal X}:\mathcal B_{\mathcal X}
       :=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\mathcal X})
       \longrightarrow\mathcal B,
 \qquad (p_{\mathcal X}^*F)(T,x)=F(T).
                                                               \tag{E.T36}
\]
All sheaves of sets on this site are included.
The functor induced by algebraic stack autoequivalences gives
an equivalence of automorphism groupoids over the indicated
base and, on classes modulo $2$-isomorphism, an isomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{Aut}_k(\mathcal M_{g,n})
       \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal B}
            (\mathcal B_{\mathcal M_{g,n}},p_{\mathcal M_{g,n}}).
                                                               \tag{E.T37}
\]
An object of the groupoid on the right is an equivalence of
topoi together with a specified isomorphism of its triangle
over $\mathcal B$; its arrows respect that isomorphism.
Thus E.T4's stable-type table is also the complete table
for (E.T37).  At the unstable types $(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0)$
the groups are, in that order, $1,1,C_2,C_2$.

The inverse in (E.T37) is actual relative reconstruction:
for every $k$-scheme $T$, with $h_T$ its represented sheaf,
\[
 \mathcal X(T)\simeq
 \operatorname{Geom}_{\mathcal B}
       (\mathcal B/h_T,\mathcal B_{\mathcal X}).
                                                               \tag{E.T38}
\]
These are groupoids, with inverse-image natural transformations
as arrows and the compatible base triangles retained.
The equivalences are pseudonatural in $T$.
Restriction to Cartesian etale sheaves is consequently the
algebraic-to-sheaf comparison of E.T12.  At $(0,2)$ and
$(1,0)$ its entire displayed $C_2$ is in the kernel.

and similarly for $L$.  The canonical map
\[
 \operatorname{Isom}(L,K)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Isom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G_K,G_L)/\operatorname{Inn}(G_L)
                                                               \tag{E.T33}
\]
is a bijection.  For a field isomorphism $\varphi:L\to K$, its image
is $g\mapsto\widetilde\varphi^{-1}g\widetilde\varphi$, where
$\widetilde\varphi:L^{\mathrm{sep}}\to K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is any
extension.  The ambiguity in this extension is exactly the indicated
inner ambiguity.  The construction is compatible with restriction
to every open subgroup and with its associated finite field extension.

statement:
Reconstruction of the full unringed topos in dimension at least three
For normal separated varieties $X,Y$ over $k$ of dimension at least
three, the map
\[
 \operatorname{Isom}_{\mathrm{schemes}}(X,Y)
   \longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Isom}(X_{\mathrm{et}},Y_{\mathrm{et}})
                                                               \tag{E.T35}
\]
is a bijection, where the right side is taken modulo natural
isomorphism and the left side allows the induced automorphism
of $k$.  In particular, every unringed topos equivalence recovers
the structure sheaf and its action on every etale object.

statement:
Full completion at residue characteristics two and three
For $p=2$ and $p=3$, put
$U_p=\mathbf P^1_{\overline{\F}_p}-\{0,1,\infty\}$.
The full geometric etale fundamental group of $U_p$ is
not isomorphic to the full completion of the topological
tripod group $F_2$.  More precisely, the explicit covers
\[
                  y^p-y=t^m,\qquad m>0,\quad p\nmid m,
 \tag{E.X1}
\]
give infinitely many linearly independent continuous
$C_p$-characters of $\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_p)$.
The exact comparison that survives is
\[
 \widehat F_2^{(p')}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
             \pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_p)^{(p')},
 \tag{E.X2}
\]
where the superscript denotes the maximal pro-prime-to-$p$
quotient.  It comes from specialization of the relative
pair $(\mathbf P^1,\{0,1,\infty\})$ over the Witt ring,
is defined up to inner automorphism after basepoints and
a specialization path are chosen, and carries each of
the three inertia groups to its corresponding inertia
group.  Thus the full-completion statements over
$\overline\Q$ used in this paper have no unchanged
specialization to either of these residue characteristics.
